To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hepatic copper storage in copper-loaded hamsters is characterized by three stages of sub-histological copper accumulation.

copper accumulation in the golden hamster hepatocyte lysosomes can be measured by energy dispersive X-ray spectrometry and that the copper binding ratio, calculated from the X-ray intensity, can be used to differentiate two sub-histochemical stages of lysosomal copper accumulation, which are characterized by different mechanisms of copper transport.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the sub-histochemical detection of copper in the lysosomes of copper loaded hamsters.
the first description of the sub-histochemical stages of copper accumulation and the identification of the corresponding transport systems.
the copper binding capacity of hepatocellular lysosomal copper and the possible role of unsaturated and saturated cuproprotesins in the copper transport process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

copper accumulation in the hepatocyte was a dynamic process and that copper was transported into the liver in the form of unsaturated cuproprotein at early stages, and as saturated cuproprotein at late stages of copper accumulation.
the three stages of copper transfer were mediated by unsaturated, partially saturated and saturated copper proteins respectively.
copper accumulation in hepatocytes was mediated by both saturated and unsaturated cupro-proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
copper was accumulated in hepatocytes in three different ways, i.e. unsaturated cuproprotein-mediated, saturated cuproprotein-mediated and copper sulphate-like complex-mediated.
the three stages of copper accumulation are the consequence of a stepwise increase of copper binding to lysosomal proteins.
copper accumulation in the hepatocyte was a continuous process and that the copper binding ratio was a reliable parameter to distinguish the three stages of sub-histological copper accumulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
copper loading can be used as a model for studying the copper accumulation in the lysosomes of hepatocytes.
copper accumulation in hepatocyte lysosomes is a dynamic process and can be divided into two stages.
the histochemical copper staining method is not sensitive enough for detecting the early stages of copper accumulation, which is a crucial step in the development of copper overload.
